general news.headline: Live: 3,000 detained, defiant CJP tells protesters to march on to Jantar MantarCJP Delhi Protest Live Updates: If you're just joining us, let's catch you up. Unprecedented scenes played out at Delhi airport, where Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and his co-convenors were detained inside their plane minutes after it landed. Much has unfolded since. At least four former chief ministers have been detained so far: Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar. With Dipke and other top leaders detained, Ajinkya Shinde is leading the CJP protest. He has urged protesters to converge at Jantar Mantar despite police action since morning that has led to around 2,000 people being detained. Meanwhile, Mamata Banerjee has begun a dharna at the police station where she is being held. To refresh our readers' memory, the CJP and the All India Students' Association (AISA) have called on supporters to gather at Jantar Mantar to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter list manipulation. With memories of the July 20 chaos and police action during the paper leak protests, which led to Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, still fresh, sweeping curbs have turned Delhi into a veritable fortress. Over 20,000 police and Central Armed Police Forces personnel have been deployed across the capital, while more than 600 people with criminal antecedents have been taken into custody. With no permission granted for the protest, police are on high alert amid fears of large-scale mobilisation. Around 150 protesters who gathered at Connaught Place, a stone's throw from Jantar Mantar, have also been detained. Will the government manage to clamp down on the stir, or will the CJP channel the stubbornness and indestructibility of its namesake to pull off Jantar Mantar 2.0? The India Today Desk will bring you the latest updates throughout the day, with reporters on the ground.
